[spoiler=Random election facts about the electoral process in Baladullah (since we just had our elections and right now there is vote recounting underway)]

-You must be 25 years old to be eligible to be a candidate for any office in Baladullah, and a citizen of at least 5 years. 

-No one can choose to run, all candidates for all offices from Neighborhood Councils to the Grand Majlisi have to be nominated by someone who knows them in person and endorsed by at least 100 signatures, or nominated by a political partys central committee. Also, the family members of the Sultan and families of the Emirs are ineligible to run for any office as a protective measure against nepotism.

-The National Electoral Commission is governed by a body made up of 2 people from every political party and an additional 3 people from the NGO Election Watch, who are approved to sit on the Commission by a majority vote in the Council of Emirs. Most of its members are volunteers, and the governing body members only make the average salary of a working person. It is regulated by the Ministry of Electoral Affairs.

-While there are phone and computer apps to vote (they require entering two forms of ID, submitting pictures of those IDs, and operate behind various levels of privacy software), most people still prefer to vote in person using either computers at voting stations or paper forms. Its a social event for some people, and often you will find (especially older) people eating snacks, drinking tea, and playing table games in adjoining areas or outside!

-Voting day is a national holiday, and by law, there must be at one voting location for every 500 people, which is large enough and has enough volunteers and computers to accommodate all theoretical 500 people in a day; voting opens at 6 am and goes until 6 pm

-Attack and smear ads are illegal, and all candidates and parties must clearly state their positions on important issues in all their literature, ads, and so forth

[/spoiler]

[list][list] [i]" Isdentai Zeten-ati Inaka, if you have chosen by happenstance or by intent to land on three-seven-six hertz, welcome to the Zetenvian National Broadcast, here we report on all matters relating to the Third Federal Republic of Ascoiya, We apologize for our sudden and abrupt end on the 17th, fear not we have managed to get our tower restored and slightly upgraded. now let us get onto the weather and then the news. [sub][pre]"It is the duty of every man to be the agent of their own fate. Our self-agency is to grant prosperity to this Ascoiyan nation. They fear the right to be happy."[/pre][/sub]

[list][sub][i]Xavier Almstedt[/i], in a meeting with Ascoiyan stakeholders in the Chamber of Commerce[/list][/sub]

[spoiler=The Chamber Parties][b]The Chamber Parties[/b]

The transition from a benighted past to a Whiggish present does not occur in a vacuum. Especially not in economic history. A nation cannot open itself up and hope that through that piecemeal openness that the future will come to them. Subsistence agriculture, the fisheries, artisanal craftmanship, these things do not generate surpluses on a scale appropriate for a modern economy. Labor is slow and ineffective, done only so that the individual may survive and not thrive. Time and time again, economic data has given to us the same movement of human economics: That in the onset of innovation, the labor necessary for the same agricultural output is reduced, which drives workers in the rural regions to seek employment in the cities.

Now here is the problem that the Ascoiyans are committing. Somare S.p.A. has provided the people with tractors, IoT systems, drones, robotic harvesters, LED lighting, hydroponics, chemical fertilizers. These have since expanded the agricultural industry of Ascoiya, with Somare executives especially targeting the province of Ouvo and its thousands upon thousands of farmers, hoping to specialize them not just in traditional cash crops but also with imported seeds to make Ascoiyan farms competitive on an international scale.

Where's the problem?

With this massive, dramatic rise in agricultural efficiency, two things have happened: First and foremost, several manual laborers in the Ouvo farms that were once considered absolutely necessary just a year ago were now easily replaceable. Somare anticipates that these workers will be out of job, preempting their need to flock to the urban cities. For this, Somare had some workarounds in place to prepare Ouvo for urbanization, working hand-in-hand with land use committees and Ascoiyan local governments to prepare factories and repair shops to help with the maintenance of Ouvo's new agricultural technology. It further helps that Ouvo already had most of the brownfield development that may be easily repurposed for Somare's manufacturing services.

The second problem is more serious. Ouvo was now projected, with very good reason, to effectively surpass the agricultural output of all other provinces in Ascoiya, spurring a massive rural flight. Ascoiya has, through its isolationism, actively worked against the Chamber of Commerce. As a result, while some manufacturing and services-related sectors were in place, it was far from the scale capable of fully absorbing this gigantic labor surplus that was soon to come. Worse still, it seemed now readily apparent that the Ascoiyans were prepared to further march headlong into the pit of its own nationalistic zeal, believing for whatever reason that the capabilities of their own citizens could hope to compete against the Five Angels.

If the Ascoiyans fear their own right to find happiness, then the Five Angels shall force it upon them! Xavier Almstedt, after a brief session of the Chamber, would agree with representatives from the other four corporations to commence what he called the "bottom-up" plan, with the five corporations setting up organizations and institutions devoted to counteracting Ascoiyan nationalism and isolationism.

In the great province of Ascoi, Almstedt Corporation would court academic intellectuals, economists, fresh graduates, and working-class laborers to form a "Many-Minded Club" (Asdej-Yarit Inat), a liberal-oriented political association to contest local elections and fill up local government posts with civil servants sympathetic to foreign corporation expansion. Through it, the corporation seeks to obtain the necessary licenses and certifications to introduce some of its more disruptive technologies in fintech, particularly credit cards and e-wallets, QR codes and crypto wallets.

Qunarco and Miwu Group, the Qianxun companies, would coordinate in the provinces of Ventona and Duven respectively. Ventona, the mineral-rich province, would be dominated by Qunarco and its steel mills, who would flood mining markets with 3D printing technologies, digital mapping, and data storage systems to make the extraction of ore and rock as safe and efficient as possible. These natural resources are then transported en masse to Duven and remade into complex alloys for use in Ascoiya's arms industry, or else into civilian appliances and automobiles to feed the pace of Ascoiyan economic growth. The Ascoiya Progressive Party (Zetenvian-Jukaen'ov Inat) would be formed by Qunarco to represent its interests in Ventona, while Miwu would do the same with the Ascoiya Liberal Constitutional Party (Zetenvian-Maokv Asevjn Inat) in Duven.

Yatenia, a central hub for Ascoiyan power, would end up under influence from Tencor with its massive "Oil Row" of tankers, causing gasoline and diesel prices in the general region to plummet after an initial spike. As the most nascent of the Five Angels, Tencor would not actually be capable of providing much in the realm of technology beyond what is already known to the Ascoiyans, and would therefore focus on fostering corporate alliances with SMEs already operating in the region. A political advocacy for this purpose, the Society for Construction and Reform (Asdeuviej-Ati Isdean'parovst Marokv) would be set up with funding and technical advice from the other Four Angels.

Last but not least, Somare which had been indirectly responsible for this whole trend. Rather than creating their own party, however, Somare executives would instead coordinate with local farming communities and unions in Ouvo, strategically merging pro-Somare groups into a single political unit, which it would call the Renovation Party (Marokv'janet Inat). Due to the limitations of the Ascoiyan language, the name would be effectively the same as if you would call it the "Whig", "Liberal", or "Reformist" Party, and so Somare would instruct those within the party to use the Llyndorran name to ensure distinctiveness in the national stage.

Together, these "chamber parties" as they were known to the Chamber Board would be instructed to shore up public support, with native party members tasked with setting up private scholarships, donation drives, career fairs, think tanks, anything and everything to help the Chamber's agenda spread like wildfire throughout Ascoiya's reluctant population.[/spoiler]

Muller was slightly amused that Elbert had decided to take out a cigar in the middle of their talks, to be fair, he didn't mind a good cigar, so he wasn't judging.

"Well I thank you for your understanding. Eagerness, with everything going on over in Tallisland. It's reasonable, I suppose, we will need to be working more closely together to support the Anti-Principalist."

A helicopter similar to the one Muller arrived on land on the tarmac, seemingly the transport that had been promised. Muller seems confused, but then remembers that the road from the airport to the city is also closed, he waves of the diplomats and gets back in the helicopter he arrived in, upon stepping into the helicopter, it was clearly a military helicopter that had been scrambled to come pick them up, there was even a forgotten ammo package that it ws carying in it. They would fly to just outside of the palace of the republic, using the road meant for military parades right out of front of it as an artificial landing pad.

The Palace of the Republic had been completed in May, a little over 7 months after ground was first broken on the building on the site of the former Royal Palace in late September. It was a shiny, new, and modernist building that housed basically the entire floueschian government as work continued across the city. out front of the building was a mini public park, with fountains that surrounded a giant statue of an unnamed revolutionary soldier. Members of the Internal Republican Guard would escort them inside the building. Its interiors also followed the same modernist style; they would have to take an elevator up to the top floor of the building. Reaching the top floor, they would reach the temporary executive floor, housing all of the offices of the various government secretariats, including the first Consul. They would take them to the office of the Muller, his office was rather simple, decorated in flags and a decent view from the window, desk in the middle of the room that was large enough for small diplomatic meetings, there was a teleophone on the desk and a collection of buttons that he could use to request the presence of the various Secretariats.
